note: CUT 64397 -> 64396 (-1, all in `schema`) by D246 item (4): the `request` description said the user decides "once (this run) or forever" where `requests.DECISIONS` has THREE allow shapes — allow_now (this run), allow_once (ONE action), allow_forever — and allow_once is offered for exactly `entities.ONCE_CLASSES`, which is what a `request` takes. Naming the missing shape cost +10 and was paid back INSIDE the same description rather than by raising the ceiling ("denies, or allows it for this run, for ONE action, or forever" replaces "decides allow/deny, once (this run) or forever"; "applies it" replaces "applies the decision"; "names one" replaces "names an entity"). The release gate caught the +10 as a red in 0.514.0's first arming, which is the test working: measure with scheduler-builder's scripts/measure_prompt_budget BEFORE arming, since no targeted test run collects this file. PREVIOUS: CUT 64454 -> 64397 (-57: harness -66, schema +9) by WP4 (P3, a guard whose fix is mechanical applies it): the memory_write bullet and the content description no longer state a 100-line CAP (a note's size is advice now, engine/memops.py, so 'the cap is then measured against the RESULT' went with it), and the wait bullet names background landings in fewer words than the old any-exit sentence; the report `detail` and wait `all` descriptions grew to say a clipped tail is never re-filed and that `all` covers background calls. PREVIOUS: RAISED 64026 -> 64454 (+428, all in `schema`) for D231: the curator may dispose of a reminder row in ANOTHER routine's store (the operator's answer, 2026-11-02: "Give rules-review a way to delete/annotate a reminder row in a DISABLED routine's store (an engine capability or a census verb), since no report can reach a routine that never runs"). The cost is spread over four descriptions of the `remind` field and buys the three things a run cannot use the op safely without: that `op=dead` exists at all and is PREFERRED over `delete` (the operator's own ordering — `dead` keeps the row's hold tally, which is the evidence its pattern was too broad, and a deletion destroys exactly that); that `target` now means the disposal ops as well as `add`, so the row acted on is in ANOTHER routine's store; and that `description` carries the REASON on a disposal rather than a caution, since the reason is stored with the annotation and is required. The first draft cost +869 and was cut to this by removing the redundancy between the four clauses — the `target` description no longer restates what `dead` keeps, and the field summary says it in one clause instead of three sentences. Nothing was added to the harness: the dial, the refusal wording and the whole rationale live in docs/reminders.md and in the OBSERVATION `remind_write.curate` returns, which only a run that actually calls it pays for. `python tests/test_prompt_budget.py --update` refuses to raise, deliberately: this was a hand edit measured against the worktree's own src, and the next CUT should lock itself in with that command. PREVIOUS: RAISED 63670 -> 64026 (+356, all in `schema`) for D198: `create_routine` gained `revises`, the flag that REVISES an existing routine's recipe instead of creating one (the operator's answer, 2026-10-19: "Add a revise path to `create_routine` (or a sibling action) gated by a per-routine dial, like `config_confirm`"). The cost is one field description, and it is the only place a run learns the three things it cannot use the path safely without: that `prompt` carries the revision (one line per change, because the TARGET's run makes the edit from those words), that the target routine's own `revise_confirm` dial decides between a decision card and an immediate hand-over, and that the edit is made by that routine's next run and never by the caller — a run that believed it was writing another routine's files would propose a diff instead of prose, and a run not told the dial exists would re-issue a proposal that is already queued. Kept to a single clause: the dial's ladder, the proposer's capability and the refusal wording all live in the OBSERVATION the handler returns (engine/reviseroutine.py), which only a run that actually calls it pays for. No harness bullet was added — `create_routine`'s own bullet already names the kind, and a second always-on sentence about a mode most runs never use is what this budget exists to refuse. `python tests/test_prompt_budget.py --update` refuses to raise, deliberately: this was a hand edit, and the next CUT should lock itself in with that command. PREVIOUS: UNCHANGED 63670 by D227 (operator, 2026-10-31: 'Why not just remaining turns, minutes, tokens (if limited)?'), recorded here because the decision WAS about this budget and paid nothing into it. A run is now told what is left of its turns, minutes and (only when limited) tokens — but on the OBSERVATION TAIL (engine/loop._tails -> turnwindow.budget_left), not in the contract: this file measures `composer.system_sections`, which is composed ONCE at run start, so a number that changes every turn would be frozen at turn 1 and a lie on every later turn. Its cost is therefore bytes x TURNS in the messages array, where nothing ratchets it, so it is measured and pinned in tests/test_budget_left_line.py instead: 46 B/turn for the common run (turns + minutes, token budget unlimited), 75 B with a token ceiling, 91 B on a resumed leg — ~14 kB over a 300-turn run, against the 63670 chars this contract re-sends on every one of those same turns. '(if limited)' is enforced literally for that reason: an unlimited axis prints nothing rather than the word 'unlimited'. PREVIOUS: CUT 63712 -> 63670 (-42: harness -51, schema +9) by the Steward hub's retirement (operator, 2026-10-28): the finish summary now comes in two labelled parts, `**Process:**` (how the run went) then `**Work:**` (the task, its conditions and consequences), and the finish bullet names where decisions go instead of a page (a blocking ask when met, the rest batched before the finish). Paid for by the finish bullet no longer restating the schema's field list and by dropping the Markdown-rendering gloss (pipe tables, quotes) from both. PREVIOUS: RAISED 62345 -> 63727 (+1382: +1008 `schema`, +374 `harness`) for D212 increment (a): one `ask_user` action may ask SEVERAL questions, and every filed decision record carries its CLASS. The cost is three things a run cannot use the feature without: the `questions` field's ask_user clause (the batch exists to be asked for), the new `blocks_work` field (the class override, whose description has to state the test it claims — `without this answer the run cannot do the work it was fired to do` — AND that it is not `mode`, because confusing the recorded class with the waiting mode is the one misreading that would make a run park itself), and the harness bullet that tells a run the batch exists at all. The first draft cost +2667; it was cut to this by dropping the justification prose from the bullet, shortening both clauses, and leaving the per-question sub-fields declared but undescribed (they mean for their question exactly what the same-named top-level field means, the way decide's items are already undescribed). What it buys back is measured, on the asking side rather than the contract: 37% of runs (60 of 163 over 282 real question records) already asked more than one question, up to 6, one action and one turn each, at a median 430 tokens of question prose per ask — so a run that batches 3 asks saves 2 turns of its own context, which is larger than 1382 chars, and the operator gets one grouped card set instead of 3 unrelated ones (51% of his answering sittings already disposed of several at once). `python tests/test_prompt_budget.py --update` refuses to raise, deliberately: this was a hand edit, and the next CUT should lock itself in with that command. PREVIOUS: RAISED 61821 -> 62345 (+524, all in `schema`) for D118 phase 3: the `background` field's description is the only place a run learns WHICH kinds may be deferred and what the ordering promise is, and phase 3 made three mutations deferrable behind a dependency barrier (engine/background_order.py). A run that is not told a write may defer, that touching the declared target is held until it lands, that a second deferred write to one target is refused and that a `then_script` may not ride a deferred change cannot use the feature safely — and the previous wording actively forbade it (`NOT available on a WRITING KIND`), so the engine accepted what every model was told to refuse.
